title: Spinach and Ricotta Ravioli
subtitle: with Tomato Sauce and Candied Seeds
description: Fast and family friendly, this dinner's just the ticket. Toss plump pasta parcels of spinach and ricotta through a tomato sauce, then sprinkle with a sweet crunch of candied seeds.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil for the ravioli. Finely chop the onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Put the sunflower seeds, ½ tsp Tuscan seasoning, 2 tsp olive oil and 2 tsp honey in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Make candied seeds: Spread the seed mixture over the lined tray. Bake for 6 mins or until golden. Meanwhile, cook the ravioli in the pan of boiling water for 5 mins or until al dente. Reserve 80ml (⅓ cup) cooking water, then drain the ravioli.

Start sauce: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 4 mins or until softened. Add the garlic and remaining Tuscan seasoning and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant. Stir in 1 tbs tomato paste.

Simmer sauce: Add the tomatoes, reserved cooking water and 1 tsp sugar (see Kitchen 101) to the onion mixture and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until thickened.

Serve up: Add the ravioli and spinach to the sauce and cook, stirring, for a further 2 mins or until warmed through and the spinach is wilted. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the ravioli among bowls. Break the candied seeds into small pieces, then scatter over the ravioli and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: Adding a little sugar to the sauce helps to balance the acidity of the tomatoes. If you prefer, you can leave the sugar out or swap for honey instead.
